title: Claiming Deceased Mutual Funds: SEBI Simplifies Transmission

faq.a: Mutual fund transmission is the process of transferring the ownership of mutual fund units from a deceased investor to their legal heir or nominee. It's a formal procedure to ensure assets pass to the rightful owner.

faq.q: How do SEBI's new rules simplify the process for nominees?
faq.a: The new rules standardise and significantly reduce the documentation required for nominees. With a valid nomination, nominees primarily need to submit the death certificate, their KYC, bank details, and a transmission request form, making the process much quicker and less cumbersome.

faq.q: What if I haven't registered a nominee for my mutual funds?
faq.a: If there is no nominee, the mutual fund units will be transmitted to the legal heirs of the deceased investor. This process typically requires legal documents like a Will, Succession Certificate, or Letter of Administration, which can be time-consuming and involve legal expenses.

faq.q: Can I nominate multiple people for my mutual funds?
faq.a: Yes, you can nominate up to three individuals for your mutual fund investments. You can also specify the percentage of units each nominee should receive.

faq.q: How long does the mutual fund transmission process typically take now?
faq.a: With a valid nomination and all required documents in order, the transmission process is expected to be completed much faster, potentially within a few weeks. Without a nomination, the timeline can extend significantly, depending on the complexity of obtaining legal heirship documents.

faq.q: What are the tax implications of mutual fund transmission?
faq.a: The transmission of mutual fund units to a nominee or legal heir upon the death of the unitholder is not considered a 'transfer' for capital gains tax purposes. Therefore, no capital gains tax is levied at the time of transmission. Tax implications arise only when the nominee/legal heir subsequently redeems or sells the units.
